sections.html:
Southwest Iowa's Cass County is about 565 square miles, with Atlantic as the county seat. Atlantic had 6,792 residents in 2020, far more than Griswold (994) or Anita (963). The county overall counted 13,127 people in 2020 and was estimated at 12,960 in 2025, with median home value around $150,300 and 71.6 percent of homes owner-occupied.

Buyers in the small towns and on rural parcels deal with the same courthouse offices as buyers in Atlantic. Rural parcels, though, carry an extra rural services levy, described below.

One building, the courthouse at 5 West 7th Street, Atlantic, IA 50022, holds every county office you will need.

  • Treasurer: 712-243-5503. Property tax counter hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and a yellow drop box sits outside the building. Online payment is available at iowatreasurers.org, and the same office processes property tax credit claims for seniors and disabled owners.
  • Assessor: 712-243-2005, open Monday to Friday from 7:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Forms and petitions can be sent to assessors@casscoia.us.
  • Auditor: works out the levy and issues the tax bill.
  • Board of Review: three or five members, independent of the assessor, who may confirm, raise or lower a value.

Homes here are assessed at 100 percent of market value on January 1, and real property gets a new valuation every other year, in the odd-numbered ones. To reach a figure the assessor weighs three approaches: comparable sales, replacement cost minus depreciation plus land, and an income method used for rentals.

Farmland is judged by what it can produce rather than by sale prices. A new building is valued by how far along it stood on January 1.

Setting rates and calculating the tax belong to other offices. What a home owes depends on its value compared with all the value in its taxing district.

The county's levy notice for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026 lists these county rates, which are normally quoted per $1,000 of taxable value.

Taxable value for general services grew from 1,187,705,773 to 1,220,800,486. City, school and other levies stack on top of these, depending on your taxing district, so ask the treasurer for the final rates on your parcel.

sections.h2: When your Cass County bill is due
sections.html:
September 1 is the due date for the first half, and it turns delinquent October 1. The second half is due March 1 and turns delinquent April 1.

Interest accrues at 1.5 percent a month, rounded to the nearest dollar, with a $1 minimum. Owners still unpaid on February 1 get a delinquent notice, and a Delinquent Tax Statement and Tax Sale Notice follows in April. Anything unpaid on May 1 picks up a publication fee and is advertised for the June sale.

Payment must be postmarked by the due date. With the parcel number you can pay even if the statement never arrived, and partial payments are accepted as long as they exceed the interest and costs.

Cass County holds its sale on the third Monday in June at 8:00 a.m., with adjourned sales on the third Monday of later months. A parcel advertised twice without a buyer moves to a Public Bidder Sale, and the county must buy it if no private bidder steps up.

Redeeming costs 2 percent per month from the sale date, and the office wants guaranteed funds. Once the county holds a Certificate of Purchase, the treasurer may also file an ordinary lawsuit to collect.

Iowa treats sold taxes as paid and puts a lien on the property. If nobody redeems within the statutory period, the certificate holder can begin tax deed proceedings, so an owner behind on taxes should act long before a deed becomes possible.

Put your protest in writing to the Board of Review during the spring window, April 2 through April 30 under Iowa Code 441.37, then take any remaining dispute to district court. The board can be asked to review equity against similar property, the value, classification, errors or fraud.

In odd-numbered years, owners whose property was changed by a state equalization order get a separate protest period. Ask the assessor for those dates.

Homestead credit and military exemption claims can be filed all year. File by July 1 and the claim applies to the current year; file later and it applies the next year.

The seller's part of the current year's tax is usually prorated and credited to the buyer, and the closing statement shows the figures.

Iowa's transfer tax is 80 cents per $500 of value above the first $500, and a declaration of value goes in with the deed. The assessor keeps the declaration for three years. Unpaid sewer or water charges that the city certified to the treasurer become a lien with the same standing as taxes, and a mobile home needs a tax clearance form before it is moved.

A seller who lives outside Iowa after the sale may owe Iowa income tax on the gain, so check that before you close.

sections.h2: Selling a house with unpaid taxes
sections.html: Many sellers do not realize an open balance is only another line on the settlement statement. Call the treasurer, learn what is owed on each half, and ask whether the parcel was sold at the June auction. If it was, the redemption figure grows by 2 percent each month, so a quick closing costs less. The title company collects the payoff from your proceeds and the treasurer releases the lien once the account is square. A cash buyer purchasing as-is does not change any of this, though it does remove repair requests from the timeline.

faqs.q: What is the Cass County property tax due date?
faqs.a: September 1 for the first half and March 1 for the second. Interest starts October 1 and April 1 at 1.5 percent monthly.

faqs.q: Where is the Cass County Treasurer?
faqs.a: In the Cass County Courthouse, 5 West 7th Street, Atlantic. Call 712-243-5503, and the property tax counter is open 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: When does Cass County hold its tax sale?
faqs.a: The third Monday in June at 8:00 a.m., with adjourned sales monthly afterward. Notices must be mailed by May 1.

faqs.q: How often does Cass County reassess property?
faqs.a: Every two years, in odd-numbered years, effective January 1. Homes are valued at 100 percent of market value.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Cass County house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid taxes and interest come out of the sale proceeds at closing. If the taxes were already sold, the redemption amount, growing at 2 percent a month, is part of the payoff.
